key_insight: Multiple disciplinary frameworks are converging into a unified view that building truly intelligent systems requires designing for physical interaction — not just prediction or simulation — combining morphology, sensing, control and learning into 'physical AI'.
problem_solved: Clarifies the gap between simulated/abstract intelligence and agents that can robustly act in the real world, reconciling fragmented perspectives and proposing a coherent research agenda and evaluation approach for physically embodied systems.
method: Synthesize frameworks from robotics, cognitive science, control theory and machine learning to identify common principles for physical agency.
Define a conceptual/operational framework that links morphology, sensing, actuation, learning and environment as the core components of physical AI.
Propose directions for metrics, benchmarks and experimental paradigms to evaluate real-world interactive competence.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical roadmap for moving systems from simulation to robust real-world operation, guiding system design, evaluation and cross-disciplinary collaboration to accelerate physically capable intelligence.
visual_elements: Venn diagram showing overlap of disciplines (robotics, neuroscience, control/ML, embodied cognition) converging on Physical AI
Closed-loop pipeline diagram: morphology ↔ sensing ↔ perception ↔ control ↔ action ↔ environment (with learning across the loop)
Table/matrix comparing existing frameworks, their strengths/limits, and unified criteria for physical competence
Icons representing sensors, actuators, learning algorithms and benchmark/testbed environments
paper_title: From embodied intelligence to physical AI
